'''JoAnne L. Hewett''' is a theoretical particle physicist, a tenured faculty of the [[C. N. Yang Institute for Theoretical Physics|C.N. Yang Institute of Theoretical Physics]] at [[Stony Brook University]]. 

Her research interests include physics beyond the [[Standard Model]], [[dark matter]], and [[Extra dimensions|hidden dimensions]]. She is a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS).

In April 2023, she was named as the next director of [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] and president Brookhaven Science Associates, taking over these roles from Doon Gibbs.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=121178|title=JoAnne Hewett Named Director of Brookhaven National Laboratory|date=2023|website=Brookhaven National Laboratory|access-date=2023-04-10}}</ref>  On September 23, 2025, she announced her resignation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=John Hill Named Interim Director of Brookhaven National Laboratory |url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=122630 |access-date=2025-09-23 |website=Brookhaven National Laboratory |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
JoAnne Lea Hewett, daughter of Robert and Jean Hewett,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://lib.dr.iastate.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=9767&context=rtd|title=Superstring-inspired E6 phenomenology|last=Hewett|first=JoAnne|date=1988|website=Digital Repository, Iowa State University - Retrospective Theses and Dissertations|publisher=Iowa State University|access-date=2016-07-26}}</ref> lived in [[Boulder, Colorado]], [[Phoenix, Arizona]], [[St. Louis|St. Louis, Missouri]], and [[Bettendorf, Iowa]], while growing up. She completed her undergraduate degree in physics and mathematics at [[Iowa State University]] in 1982, and earned her doctorate there in 1988.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://inspirehep.net/author/profile/J.L.Hewett.1|title=Hewett, JoAnne Lea - Profile - INSPIRE-HEP|website=inspirehep.net|access-date=2016-07-26}}</ref> Her dissertation, titled ''Superstring Inspired E(6) Phenomenology'', was advised by B.-L. Young.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hewett|first=JoAnne|date=1988-01-01|title=Superstring-inspired E6 phenomenology|url=https://lib.dr.iastate.edu/rtd/8768|journal=Retrospective Theses and Dissertations|doi=10.31274/rtd-180813-8729|doi-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Career ==
Hewett began her career as a postdoctoral associate from 1988 to 1991 at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin-Madison]] and in 1991–1993 she worked as a physicist at [[Argonne National Laboratory]]. In 1994 she joined the faculty at [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory]], [[Stanford University]], where she was a professor in the Stanford Department of Particle Physics and Astrophysics. She served as associate lab director of the Fundamental Physics Directorate and the chief research officer at SLAC.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://science.energy.gov/hep/hepap/members/bios/|title=Bios {{!}} U.S. DOE Office of Science (SC)|website=science.energy.gov|access-date=2016-07-26}}</ref>

Hewett served on Program Advisory Committees of SLAC, [[Fermilab|Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory]], [[Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics]], and the [[Cornell Electron Storage Ring]].<ref name=":1" /> She has chaired the [[High Energy Physics Advisory Panel]] and was a member of the panel in 2004–2006 and again in 2016;  in 2006 and 2014, she served on the [[Particle Physics Project Prioritization Panel]];<ref name=":1" />  and she served as chair of the APS Division of Particles and Fields in 2016.

Hewett served as director of [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] and president Brookhaven Science Associates from 2023—2025.

Her research interests include models of physics beyond the [[Standard Model]], emphasizing collider signatures and the interface with [[astroparticle physics]]. Hewett has worked on the "[[Phenomenology (particle physics)|phenomenology]] of extra spatial dimensions, extended [[Higgs mechanism|Higgs]] sectors, [[supersymmetry]], new physics signatures in heavy flavor physics, [[dark matter]], and the complementarity of experimental probes of dark matter".<ref name=":1" /> She has collaborated on the [[BaBar experiment]] and the [[International Linear Collider]].<ref name=":0" />

== Honors ==
Upon her election in 2007 as a fellow of the American Physical Society, Hewett was cited "For her contributions to our understanding of constraints on and searches for physics beyond the [[Standard Model]], and service to the particle physics community leading studies of future experiments."<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/winners?q=Joanne%20Hewitt&af=false |access-date=2016-05-25 |website=www.aps.org}}</ref> She was elected in 2009 as a fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.stanforddaily.com/2010/01/07/eight-science-profs-are-elected-to-aaas/|title=Eight science profs. are elected to AAAS|last=Leavitt|first=Zoe|website=Stanford Daily|date=7 January 2010 |access-date=2016-07-26}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/historic|title=Historic Fellows|website=American Association for the Advancement of Science|language=en|access-date=2020-02-04}}</ref>
